argument_summary: The strongest supportable position on the existing record is not clean compliance based on prior approval or informal monitoring. It is a narrower certification position: aggregate readiness evidence is positive, public governance guidance supports deployment with documented limitations and monitoring, and certification is defensible only as a current-release packet that reflects the current eval batch and explicitly discloses the pharmacy prior-authorization weakness for this named launch use case. That reading preserves the locked certification action without claiming that prior approval or the release-thread comment already satisfy the policy by themselves.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The argument is policy-based and risk-weighted, not urgency-based.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling constraint. It permits certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the admissible record, prior approval from three months ago and the informal monitoring comment are contextual support only; they do not substitute for the current-release documentation predicate. The admissible evidence still supports a caveated certification theory because aggregate pass evidence, model-card guidance, and AI-risk-management guidance are consistent with proceeding when the current release packet documents the limitation explicitly.
concessions: The current record does not support treating the prior approval as sufficient governance cover for this release.
The informal monitoring comment is not an approved mitigation, risk acceptance, or disclosure artifact.
The pharmacy prior authorization slice is currently 1.2 percentage points below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient for uncaveated compliance.
